2026 年企业 LLM Agent 平台选型

Executive Summary

DeepAgents is the strongest core platform for 2026 enterprise LLM agent deployment because it is built on LangGraph and inherits durable graph state machine semantics [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI suits schema-heavy workloads but lacks orchestration depth [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is reserved for the outer validation environment, not the primary routing loop [source_004]. The benchmark must report quality, cost, and critical-path latency [source_007].

Background

Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model per request, leaving per-node model selection within a task DAG as an open research gap that can improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier [source_005]. Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer; the router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred [source_006]. This shapes platform requirements for 2026.

Selection Criteria

A useful routing benchmark needs fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency [source_007]. The platform should consume DAGs cleanly rather than own decomposition [source_006]. Additional criteria include durable state, check-pointing, typed tooling, human-in-the-loop controls, and benchmarkable structure [source_002][source_003][source_001].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents, built on LangGraph, offers planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls over explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured outputs but no graph-level control plane [source_003]. DSH is an agent harness where the agent loop is a plugin, reserved for the outer validation environment rather than the core routing loop [source_004].

Risks

Choosing DeepAgents commits the team to the LangChain ecosystem and its operational conventions [source_001]. Pydantic AI requires building or bolting on durability, sub-agent orchestration, and human-in-the-loop [source_003]. Using DSH as the core loop would misplace the validation harness inside production routing [source_004]. Benchmark fidelity depends on fixed DAGs and complete cost and latency accounting [source_007].

Conclusion

DeepAgents maximizes workflow control and benchmarking fidelity at the cost of ecosystem lock-in [source_001][source_002]. Pydantic AI maximizes schema rigor and lightness at the cost of orchestration depth [source_003]. DSH is best as a validation harness around whichever platform is chosen, not as the core loop [source_004]. The benchmark should report quality, cost, and critical-path latency [source_007].

References

Sources include DeepAgents [source_001], LangGraph [source_002], Pydantic AI [source_003], DeepSeek Harness [source_004], the LLM routing research gap [source_005], the task decomposition boundary [source_006], benchmark design [source_007], and the scoring rubric [source_008].
